defect.description: The edge case where new_mobject is old_mobject: the new deduplication removes the object from the list before searching, so scene.replace(a, a) no longer finds a, raises ValueError and leaves a removed from the scene; the deduplication must skip the case new_m is old_m (or run only after the replacement).
defect.location: src/scene.py (the deduplication at the top of replace_in_list)

review_items: scene.py:37-38 dedup guard removes new_m from unrelated list on recursive calls (cross-level replace destroys top-level reference)
scene.py:37-38 when old_mobject is new_mobject, guard removes object before search, causing ValueError on replace(a, a)
test_scene.py:37 missing test for cross-level nesting scenario
test_scene.py nit: no test for self-replacement replace(x, x)
votes.evidence_quote: When `old_mobject is new_mobject`, the guard removes the object from the list before the search loop, so `replace_in_list` returns `False` and the `ValueError("Could not find …")` fires.
votes.justification: The second finding names the exact defect. In replace_in_list, the deduplication removes the object before the search, so scene.replace(a, a) raises a ValueError instead of being a no-op.
